newsitem.title: JAMAICA: ADM extends takeover bid for Jamaican flour mill.
newsitem.headline: ADM extends takeover bid for Jamaican flour mill.

text.p: ADM Milling, a unit of Archer Daniels Midland Co, placed full-page ads in local papers Monday announcing that it was extending its buyout offer for Jamaica Flour Mills until June 12.
The offer had been set to expire at the end of business Tuesday.

A heated battle has been waged in recent weeks between company management and ADM for control of JFM, the country's only flour mill. Management was claiming victory, saying it had enough shareholder commitment to block the takeover.

Earlier this year, ADM offered $35 million for 100 percent of JFM shares, but later raised the offer to $40.77 million. JFM's chairman, Henry Fullerton, offered his 38 percent holding and undertook to find another 22 percent.
ADM said it first needed to take 60 percent and would then make an offer for full control of the company.

But a number of shareholders said ADM's offer was half the book value of the company and did not take into account JFM's $10 million in cash reserves and another $20 million the company expects to receive from a recent court ruling.

The company's management said it would offer 80 percent of this $20 million, after taxes, to shareholders. ADM said it intends to keep the cash. The management said it has commitments from shareholders of over 45 percent of the total shares, enough to block ADM's offer.
The management is also undertaking to find new overseas buyer's for Fullerton's 38 percent, which he wants to sell to pay down debts he acquired in part when he bought the shares several years back.
On Sunday, JFM employees ran a full-page ad backing the management and urging shareholders to reject ADM's offer.
JFM is traded on the Kingston stock exchange.
